# BackButton

Figma: [06i. BackButton](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-939) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-15

The Syntropy returning-navigation control - a preset over Button / IconButton, plus an on-media treatment for hero & dark headers. 120 variants: Emphasis × Type × Size × State × Direction, with a line arrow (← / →) and an editable label for “Back to {destination}”.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/back-button/reference.png`

### BackButton

Preset over Button/IconButton (Variant=tertiary) for returning to the previous screen or step, with a mirrored arrow (Back / رجوع) and an On-media white variant for hero images.

Level: molecule · Contains: Button, IconButton · Part of: AppBar

Use when:
- Leading slot of a header or inline above content on detail screens and wizard steps
- Back over a deal hero photo or dark header (Emphasis=On-media)
- Dense headers (Type=Icon only)

Don't use when:
- Showing location across levels: use Breadcrumb
- Switching sibling views: use SegmentedTabs or TabBar
- Dismissing an overlay: use the SheetHeader close
- When the AppBar already shows a back arrow: keep one back affordance per screen

Accessibility: Icon only needs aria-label Back / رجوع; keep the focus ring; hide rather than disable on the first screen of a flow.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

BackButton is the Syntropy pattern for returning to the previous screen or step. It is not a new control - it is a thin, opinionated preset of the existing Button and IconButton, so it inherits every state, size, focus ring and token they already define.

### When to use

- Returning one level up in a flow - a detail screen, a wizard step, a nested settings page.
- In an AppBar / header leading slot, or inline above page content.

### When not to use

- Showing where the user is across levels - use Breadcrumb (06f).
- Switching between sibling views - use TabBar (06b).
- Dismissing an overlay - use the Modal / Drawer close affordance.

### Atomic architecture

BackButton composes real design-system components rather than redrawing them. Update Button or IconButton once and every BackButton updates with it.

- Label type → Button, Variant=tertiary - the neutral ghost button, with a leading icon and the “Back” / “رجوع” label.
- Icon-only type → IconButton, Variant=tertiary - for dense headers where the label is implied.
- Leading glyph → Icon / Back3, the Back3 back line-arrow; a flat mirrored sibling is used for RTL so it points the right way.
- The arrow stroke is bound to icon/default (to match the text/default label), so glyph and text always match - light and dark mode alike.

### Anatomy

- Leading arrow - Icon / Back3 at 12px, tinted with the label colour. Points left in LTR, right in RTL.
- Label - “Back” (LTR) / “رجوع” (RTL), in the host button's text style. Hidden in the Icon-only type.
- Hit area - inherited from Button / IconButton padding; clears the 44×44 minimum target at Size = md.
- Focus ring - the host button's focus ring, never removed.

### Variants - Type

### Label

The default. Icon plus text - best when space allows and a word makes the destination clearer.

### Icon only

Glyph alone, for compact headers - it matches the AppBar back affordance. Always provide an aria-label (“Back”).

### Sizes - web & mobile

Every type and direction ships in three sizes, inherited straight from Button / IconButton. Choose by surface, not by whim.

- lg - prominent web headers, onboarding and marketing flows where the back affordance should be effortless to hit with a cursor.
- md - the default for most web screens and a comfortable touch target.
- sm - dense mobile headers, toolbars and compact cards where space is tight.
- Match the BackButton size to its neighbours - the AppBar title, or the screen's primary button.

### Emphasis - text & on-media

Two emphases cover where a back control lives - pick by the surface behind it.

### Standard

- The default - composed from the real Button / IconButton (Variant=tertiary). Neutral, for normal surfaces.

### On-media

- A white glyph and label on a translucent dark scrim - for back-over-hero-image and dark headers (deal-detail, onboarding). The one hand-tinted exception, since the system has no inverse Button variant; scrim deepens on hover/pressed.

### States

States are inherited from the host Button / IconButton - not re-implemented. Change the nested instance's State, or wire it to interaction states in code.

- Default - neutral glyph and label.
- Hover / pressed - the host button's hover and pressed treatments.
- Focused - a visible focus ring for keyboard users.
- Disabled - muted, and only when going back is genuinely unavailable. Prefer hiding the control over disabling it.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Set Direction on the BackButton - it maps straight to the host button's Direction. The arrow is mirrored, not rotated: LTR points left, RTL points right, both meaning “go back”.

- LTR - arrow leads on the left, label “Back”.
- RTL - arrow leads on the right, label “رجوع” set in Noto Sans Arabic.

### Behavior

- Activating it pops the current screen or step - the same outcome as the platform back gesture.
- Keep the label short and literal (“Back”), or name the destination (“Back to Portfolio”) when that helps.
- On the first screen of a flow there is nothing to return to - hide the control rather than disabling it.
- One back affordance per screen - don't pair an inline BackButton with a header back arrow.

### Code examples

### HTML · ARIA

```dart
<button class="back-btn" aria-label="Back">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><!-- Icon / Back3 --></svg>
  <span>Back</span>
</button>

<!-- RTL: dir="rtl" mirrors the arrow; label becomes رجوع -->
<button class="back-btn" dir="rtl" aria-label="رجوع">
  <svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><!-- mirrored --></svg>
  <span>رجوع</span>
</button>
```

### Usage - Do and Don’t

Do

Do use a short, literal label - “Back”, or name the destination (“Back to Portfolio”) when it adds clarity.

Don’t

Don't disable the back button on the first screen of a flow - hide it; there is nothing to return to.

Do

Do let Direction flip the arrow - “رجوع” with the arrow leading on the right in RTL.

Don’t

Don't pair an inline BackButton with a header back arrow - keep one back affordance per screen.

### In this system

- Button - text variant (labelled base)
- IconButton - icon-only base
- AppBar (06a) - header back affordance
- Breadcrumb (06f) - cross-level navigation

### Notes from the maintainer

Built 2026-06-15. BackButton is deliberately a preset over the existing Button / IconButton rather than a bespoke control - so it can never drift from the system's button states, tokens or focus behaviour. The leading glyph is Icon / Back3 (your pick over the chevron); RTL uses a flat mirrored sibling because Figma won't flip a nested instance in place, and the arrow stroke is bound to icon/default (matching text/default) so the two never disagree. If the icon-only type ever feels too quiet in a header, reach for the AppBar's leading slot instead. - Abdulrahman
